newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY PARLIAMENT UNANIMOUSLY WELCOMES NATO INVITE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY PARLIAMENT UNANIMOUSLY WELCOMES NATO INVITE.

text.p: Hungary's parliament unanimously passed on Tuesday a motion welcoming the decision by the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation last week to invite Hungary into the first group of new members.
In an almost unprecedented show of unity between government and opposition parties the house passed the motion with 312 votes for, none against and no abstentions.

"The Parliament of the Hungarian Republic welcomes the results of the NATO summit meeting in Madrid and is convinced that...the resolution enlarging NATO promotes the democratic development of the region and strengthens the stability and the security of Europe," the resolution said.

A NATO summit in Madrid last week invited Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic to become the first new members of an expanded alliance and reassured Slovenia, Romania and the Baltic States that they would be considered seriously in future expansions.

"This invitation is a recognition of all that Hungary has achieved in its democratic transformation, its social and economic development, in the building a market economy and the creation of stability in Central and Eastern Europe," the parliamentary statement said.
It added that negotiations for membership will speed up the development of the Hungarian armed forces and result in the "liquidation of the remnants of the Cold War."
The motion expressed Hungary's desire to see further expansion of the alliance to include other countries which applied for membership but did not make the first group.
It also authorised the government to hold a national referendum by the end of November "to sound out the opinion of the people".
The referendum is non-binding and would therefore not prevent the government going ahead with accession should it result in a "No" vote.

However analysts say such an outcome is highly unlikely. The most recent opinion poll, taken before Madrid, showed 65 percent of those polled in favour of NATO membership, a rise of over 15 percentage points on previous surveys. REUTER
